comparison: Both evaluate the reporter mouse generation and validation (C4, C19, C25, C29-C31). OpenEval finds claims fully supported by methodological data and supplements. Peer reviewers also accept this as 'an important new resource' but request clarifications about 2A peptide mechanism and antigen presentation validation (revisions 20-22). Strong agreement on core finding with peer review seeking additional technical details.

Perfect alignment on spleen characterization claims (C32-C39). Both find flow cytometry and immunostaining data supporting expected expression patterns. OpenEval notes correlation between tdT and MHC II expression. Peer reviewers accept the data while asking about magnitude differences between reporters (revision 3), indicating acceptance with interest in interpretation.

Complete agreement on in vitro validation (C41-C42). Both accept IFN-γ induction data from OPC cultures as validating reporter responsiveness to inflammatory stimuli. Peer reviewer request for higher magnification images (revision 30) indicates interest in examining details rather than questioning the finding.

Both support baseline CNS expression characterization (C43-C48). OpenEval emphasizes extensive tissue imaging showing distinct patterns and neuronal B2m expression. Peer reviewers accept core observations but request clarification about specific cell types and anatomical details (revisions 25-29), seeking better documentation rather than challenging findings.

Agreement on EAE model findings (C51-C56). OpenEval finds tissue imaging and flow cytometry with appropriate statistics support correlation between disease severity and reporter expression. Peer reviewers accept demonstration of reporters' utility in inflammatory models while requesting better image resolution and anatomical orientation (revisions 14, 25-27).

Divergence on oligodendroglia quantification (C59-C69). OpenEval finds claims supported by quantitative immunohistochemistry with adequate statistics and sample sizes. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting 'differences observed are borderline significant and very variable' (revision 9) and discrepancies with published frequencies (revision 7). Agreement on presence of immune oligodendroglia but disagreement on quantitative robustness.

Agreement on OPC findings (C70-C74). Both accept that immune oligodendroglia are predominantly mature cells and that immune OPCs are not depleted. OpenEval notes inference is reasonable though longitudinal studies would strengthen it. Peer reviewers accept findings but request discussion of implications (revision 8).

Agreement on astrocyte expression (C75-C76). Both accept immunostaining data showing reporter expression in astrocytes. OpenEval notes functional significance not quantified. Peer reviewers request more discussion and better integration into narrative (revision 23). Both see value but want more development.

Strong agreement on brain tissue and AT-CUP model findings (C77-C82, C83, C85-C88). OpenEval finds brain analysis with appropriate statistics supports differential correlations between reporters. Peer reviewers accept versatility demonstration and regional enrichment in inflammatory areas without challenge. Both validate reporters work across multiple disease models and regions.

OpenEval R10 addresses AT-CUP model validation (C83-C88) which overlaps with peer R9 coverage. OpenEval emphasizes regional ratio analysis controlling for variability. Peer reviewers accept the AT-CUP data as part of demonstrating system versatility across models.

Divergence on scRNA-seq experimental design (C89-C99). OpenEval finds claims supported with appropriate quality metrics, acknowledging technical limitations. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about n=1 biological replicate (revision 10), tissue choice (revision 31), and potential underrepresentation of stressed oligodendroglia. Agreement on data quality but disagreement on experimental robustness.

Divergence on oligodendroglia subclustering analysis (C100-C110). OpenEval finds detailed scRNA-seq analysis with appropriate cluster validation supports claims, noting analytical rigor in removing contaminating clusters. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting further subclustering (revision 11), statistical validation with p-values (revision 33), and expansion of PD-L1 discussion (revision 32). OpenEval sees methodological strength; peer reviewers need more statistical detail.

Strong agreement on dataset integration (C111-C117). OpenEval finds integrated analysis showing reproducibility across datasets supports claims. Peer reviewers specifically requested this integration (revision 10) and acceptance indicates it successfully addresses concerns. Both see this as strengthening and validating the immune oligodendroglia populations identified.

Strong agreement on overarching conclusions (C118-C120, C127). OpenEval finds key findings supported by collective data. Peer reviewers explicitly endorse conclusions as 'compelling demonstration' and 'important new resource.' Both agree on core utility and significance despite some specific quantitative details being questioned elsewhere.

OpenEval evaluates background/rationale claims (C1-C3, C6-C12, C17-C18) as accurately summarizing knowledge gaps with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviews typically focus on novel findings rather than literature review accuracy.

OpenEval evaluates established knowledge citations about B2m and Cd74 (C21-C28, C36, C40) as accurate and appropriately supporting reporter target selection. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval rates speculative/future direction claims (C13-C16, C50, C106, C121-C122, C124-C126, C128-C129) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are appropriately qualified but not directly tested. Peer reviewers touch on C106 (PD-L1) in R11 requesting expansion of discussion, but no comprehensive peer evaluation of speculative claims as a group.

OpenEval evaluates citations about MHC expression in other CNS contexts (C123, C130-C135) as supported, noting demonstration of reporter expression in multiple cell types supports broader utility claims. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature-based claims.
